description: Recommends four-year tax phase-in for multi-residential, non-residential.
Recommends two-year tax phase-in for other residential properties.
Aims to smooth property tax changes from reassessment.

chips.text: Chair noted phase-in prevents wild swings in property tax system.
Property owners with increasing assessments benefit from phase-in.
Councillor Pearce opposed, citing unfair taxation for those losing property value.

description: Committee recommends 1.75:1 non-residential to residential tax ratio for 2025-2029.
Median single-family homes would see a 10.2% tax increase.
Some commercial properties would see tax decreases, others increases.

chips.text: Jason Aebig argued changing the ratio sends the wrong message and creates business unpredictability.
Multi-residential properties face over 30% tax increase without rebalancing.
The Chamber questioned if the 1.43 ratio's underlying principles still apply today.
Greater Saskatoon Chamber of Commerce opposed the proposed tax ratio change.
Councillor Jeffries voted against the 1.75 ratio, preferring a 1.88 revenue-neutral option.
Administration will engage community and stakeholders on overall tax policy guidelines and goals.

speakers.name: Jason Aebig, Greater Saskatoon Chamber of Commerce
said: Proposed ratio change works against the 2013 goal of 1.43.
Hasty changes create uncertainty for businesses, still reeling from 2021.
Tax ratio policy should be part of a grounded, forward-thinking growth plan.

description: Committee recommends approving 2025 budgets for five Business Improvement Districts.
These budgets determine levies charged to commercial properties within BID areas.
Levy increases range from 0% to 14.3% for 2025.

chips.text: Councillor Dubois questioned why Council approves BID budgets if they don't affect the city budget.
Administration will review if BID budget approvals can become information reports.

description: Recommend adding $40,000 to 2025 residential property tax levy.
Recommend adding $250,000 to 2025 multi-residential property tax levy.
Recommend adding $3,000,000 to 2025 commercial/industrial property tax levy.
Approves land exchange for Hampton Village Business Park development.
Allocates developable land proportionally among five landowners.
Allows Mamawi Holdings to retain 10.85 acres of raw land.

chips.text: Another landowner, Dream, provided dedicated lands for Mamawi Holdings.

description: Recommends transferring $11.7 million surplus to Fiscal Stabilization Reserve.
Recommends $158,798 to Printing and Mail Equipment Reserve.
Recommends $414,528 to Self-Insured Retention Reserve.

chips.text: CFO Hack explained one-time surplus funding is unsuitable for ongoing transit service increases.
Committee's recommendation for printer reserve transfer is an unusual, fiscally prudent anomaly.
Sherry Terrassoth submitted questions about using surplus for transit service improvements.

description: Committee recommends adjusting budgets for $1.376 million in federal green funding.
Funding supports bioreactor, building retrofits, and water conservation projects.
Water conservation project could save $254,000 annually after three years.

chips.text: Councillor noted $254,000 annual savings from water project was not in report.

description: Sets the 2025-26 audit plan for city operations.
Includes six audits on cybersecurity and procurement.
Committee recommends $225,000 for Downtown Event District property repairs.
Funds would come from the Property Realized Reserve.
Repairs include roof, AC, and access control at 39 23rd Street.

chips.text: CFO Hack clarified lease profits repay internal loan for property purchases.

description: Apply for $160 million federal funding for new water mains.
Seek $427,000 federal grant for commercial building retrofits.

chips.text: Councillor asked about probability and strategic funding for the $160 million application.
Residents and commercial building owners could benefit from federal funding.
Deep Retrofit Initiative aims to advance decarbonization plans for commercial buildings.
Administration will report back to committee by summer on application success.

description: Recommends 10-year SaskTel cell tower lease in Churchill Park.
Lease at 1015 Wilson Crescent generates $16,892 annually.

chips.text: SaskTel will continue operating its cell tower in Churchill Park.

description: Recommends purchasing 13 acres for a Holmwood high school/leisure centre.
The land costs $10,842,000 from Dream Asset Management.

chips.text: CFO Hack confirmed the $10.8M land price includes a 15% discount from fair market value.
Future students and residents of the Holmwood area will benefit from the new facilities.

description: Approves five-year digital billboard license with Pattison Outdoor.
City receives $25,500 annually for five years.
Billboard located adjacent to Circle Drive, west of Avenue C.

chips.text: Council previously directed renegotiation for a five-year term instead of seven years.

description: Committee recommends appointing Mayor Block as proxy.
Proxy to vote at Centennial Auditorium AGMs.
Meetings are on April 25, 2025.
